elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: The inserted sentence warrants only that Hosting and Support Services will "conform in all material respects to the requirements of this Agreement" for 30 days; no professional/workmanlike standard appears anywhere in Section 9, and Sections 3 and 4 impose only "reasonable commercial efforts."

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "the Interface and all related software will conform in all material respects to its documentation."

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Inserted period is "ninety (90) days following delivery," not 12 months.
Inserted services period is "thirty (30) days following performance," short of 90 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "TrueLink will, at Client's election, repair or replace the non-conforming software or Services..."
Inserted: "...or refund the fees paid for the non-conforming software or Services."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty was added; Section 9 as rendered contains only the Y2K warranty plus the new conformance warranty.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious code / virus warranty appears in the rendered language.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Express software-to-documentation warranty inserted: "for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, the Interface and all related software will conform in all material respects to its documentation" — the Interface and related software are expressly software, satisfying the software-specific requirement.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "for a period of thirty (30) days following performance, the Hosting Services and Support Services will conform in all material respects to the requirements of this Agreement" — both service categories are defined terms and the period meets the 30-day floor.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "TrueLink will, at Client's election, repair or replace the non-conforming software or Services" — remedy applies to both the software and services warranties ("For any breach of this warranty").
"...or refund the fees paid for the non-conforming software or Services."

reasons: Finding status "deviation" is correct: the only pre-existing TrueLink warranty (Section 9) is a Y2K date-processing warranty, and Sections 3/4 impose only "reasonable commercial efforts," so before the edit no fallback element was met (no software-to-documentation warranty, no services warranty period, no repair/replace/refund remedy).
All four fallback elements are met in operative language by the single inserted sentence pair; the fallback level is position-complete.

Preferred level is incomplete: no professional-and-workmanlike standard, 90 days rather than 12 months for software, 30 days rather than 90 days for services, no compliance-with-laws warranty, and no malicious-code warranty. The drafter must add those five items in operative text to reach the preferred position.

Minimality holds: a concise insertion into the existing Section 9 for a missing clause, no deletion or paraphrase of existing text, no survival tail, no procedural or expense boilerplate, and the pre-existing Y2K warranty and its Client-favourable "at TrueLink's sole cost and expense" language are retained. The disclaimer at p0076 is already prefaced "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT," so correctly no carve-out edit was made.

Note (not a minimality failure): the remedy is drafted "at Client's election" whereas the playbook model language gives the choice "at Vendor's option." The checklist element is silent on who elects, so this stays within the element, but it is a more aggressive posture than the model and is the likely negotiation give if TrueLink pushes back.

Note (not an element failure): the services warranty is measured against "the requirements of this Agreement," and those requirements are themselves only "reasonable commercial efforts" in Sections 3 and 4, so the 30-day services warranty adds limited substantive teeth. If more bite is wanted, anchor it to the professional-and-workmanlike standard (which would also close a preferred-level gap).

Intent preserved: the Y2K warranty, its evidence/repair mechanic, and the disclaimer survive without contradiction; "Interface," "Hosting Services" and "Support Services" are defined terms and no cross-reference is left dangling.
